Short title, extent and application

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART I‑PRELIMINARY
1. Short title, extent and application.‑(1) This Ordinance
may be called the West Pakistan Pure Food Ordinance, 1960.
(2) It extends to the whole of
the Province of West Pakistan, except the Federal Capital and the Special
Areas.
(3) It shall come into
operation in respect of such foods or generally in respect of such areas as
Government may by notification direct.

Definitions

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART I‑PRELIMINARY
2. Definitions.‑In this Ordinance, unless the context otherwise
requires, the following expressions shall have the meanings hereby respectively
assigned to them; that is to say‑
"(a) "banaspati" means any article of food which
resembles ghee and is derived from vegetable fat and contains no milk or animal
fat ;
(b) "butter" means
the substance usually known as butter, made exclusively from cow or buffalo
milk, or from cream or dahi prepared
from such milk, with or without salt or other preservative or with or without
the addition of colouring matter ;
(c) "charbini" means any article of food which resembles
ghee or banaspati, but contains
animal fat other than milk fat ; .
(d) "cream or balai" means that portion of milk
rich in milk fat which rises to the surface of milk on standing or which has
been separated by skimming or otherwise, and is meant for human consumption ;
(e) "dahi" means the product obtained by lactic acid
fermentation of milk ;
(f) "Director" means
Director of Health Services, West Pakistan, and includes any person specially
empowered for the purposes of this Ordinance by Government who for the time
being performs the duties of that office ;
(g) "food" means any
article used as food or drink for human con sumption, other than drugs or
water, and includes‑
(i) any substance which is
intended for use in the composition or preparation of food ;
(ii) any flavouring matter or
condiment ;
(iii) any colouring matter
intended for use in food ; and
(iv) chewing gum and other
products of the like nature.
Explanation I.‑Water shall be deemed to be food if it is
intended for use in the composition or preparation of food.
Explanation II.‑An article shall not cease to be food by
reason only that it is also capable of being used as a medicine.
(h) "ghee" means ghee prepared exclusively from butter ;
(i) "Government"
means the. Government of West Pakistan;
(j ) "Inspector"
means an Inspector appointed under this Ordinance ;
(k) "margarine" means
any food, whether mixed with butter or not, which resembles butter and is not
milk‑blended butter ;
(l) "milk" means the
normal, clean and pure secretion obtained from the udders of a cow, buffalo,
sheep or a goat from which cream has not been extracted, and includes boiled,
pasteurised and sterilized milk ;
(m) "occupier" means
the person who has control of the affairs of a factory and includes the manager
or managing agent or any other person authorised to represent the occupier ;
(n) "package" includes every article in which goods for
carriage or for sale are cased, covered, enclosed, contained or packed ;
"(o) "pre‑packed"
means packed or made up in advance ready for retail sale in a wrapper or
container ;
(p) "prescribed"
means prescribed by rules made under this Ordi nance ;
(q) "Public Analyst"
means an Analyst appointed under this Ordinance ;
(r) "retail sale" means any sale to a person buying
otherwise than for the purpose of re‑sale, but does not include a sale to
a caterer for the purposes of his catering business, or a sale to a
manufacturer‑for the purposes of his manufacturing business ;
(s) "sale" means a
transfer of ownership in exchange for a price paid or promised or part paid or
part promised, and includes barter, and refers only to sale for human
consumption or use ;
(t) "skimmed milk" means milk" which after
extraction of milk fat by mechanical or other process contains such fat in
quantity less than 3 per cent. and includes separated milk ;
(u) "standardised
milk" means milk from cow or buffalo standardised to contain not less than
12.4 per cent. of milk solids, including 3.5 per cent. of milk fat, provided
that the term "standardised" refers to the standard isation of fat
contents alone ;
(v) "transit"
includes all stages' of transit from the dairy, place of manufacture or other
source of origin to the consumer ; and
(w) "wholesale" means
any sal

False warranty

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
II‑GENERAL PROVISIONS
3. False warranty.‑No person shall in respect of any food
sold by him or given by him for sale to an agent give to the purchaser or his
agent a false warranty in writing.

Prohibition of mixing and selling mixed food

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
II‑GENERAL PROVISIONS
4. Prohibition of mixing and
selling mixed food,‑(1) No person shall mix, colour, stain or powder
or direct or permit any other person to mix, colour, stain or powder any food
with any matter or ingredient‑
(a) in contravention of the prescribed rules ; or
(b) so as to render the food injurious to health with intent that
the same may be sold in that state.
(2) No person shall sell, offer, keep or store any food so mixed,
coloured, stained or powdered.

Prohibition of sale, preparation, manufacture, import of export of unwholesome food intended for human consumption

WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
II‑GENERAL PROVISIONS
5. Prohibition of sale, preparation or manufacture of unwholesome food
intended for human consumption.‑No person shall, directly or
indirectly, himself or by any other person, sell, keep or store any food
intended for human consumption or prepare or manufacture any such food, with
intent that the same may be sold, which is unsound, unwholesome, injurious to
health or unfit for human consumption.

Prohibition of sale or manufacture for sale of food which is adulterated or misbranded or not of the nature, substance or quality demanded

WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
II‑GENERAL PROVISIONS
6. Prohibition of sale or manufacture for sale of food not of the
proper nature, substance or quality.‑No person shall, directly or
indirectly, himself or by any other person‑
(a) sell any food which is not
of the nature, substance or quality demanded.; or
(b) manufacture, sell, offer,
keep or store any food which is not of the nature, substance or quality which
it purports or is represented to be ; or
(c) import, manufacture, sell,
offer, keep or store any food notified in this behalf by Government, unless it
is coloured in the manner prescribed; or,
(d) import any food in such
manner or in such condition as renders it or is likely to render it injurious
to health.

Sale of pre-packed food

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
II‑GENERAL PROVISIONS
7. Sale of pre‑packed food.‑No person shall sell any
pre‑packed food unless he has complied with such rules as may be
prescribed in this behalf.

Prohibition of sale of food without complying with rules

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
II‑GENERAL PROVISIONS
8. Prohibition
of sale of food without complying with rules.‑No person shall import,
manufacture, sell, offer for sale, keep or store any food specified in this behalf,
unless the rules prescribed for the mode of its manufacture, processing or
preparation, packaging, labelling, consignment, delivery, grade designation or
fill of containers have been complied with.

Sale of margarine, banaspati and charbi

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
II‑GENERAL PROVISIONS
9. Manner in which margarine, banaspati or charbini may be sold.‑(1)
No person shall sell, whether wholesale or retail, or forward by any public
conveyance any margarine, banaspati or
charbini, unless every package
containing margarine, banaspati or charbini, whether open or closed, bears
the words "Margarine", "Banaspati"
or "Charbini", as the
case may be, durably marked in such manner as may be prescribed ; and in the
case of charbini the nature of fat
from which the charbini has been
produced shall be clearly indicated.
(2) No person selling
margarine, banaspati or charbini shall describe the substance
being sold, on any wrapper enclosing it, or on any package containing it, or on
any label attached to a parcel thereof, or in any advertisement or invoice
thereof, by any name other than margarine, banaspati
or charbini, as the case may be,
or a name combining the word "Margarine", "Banaspati" or "Charbini",
as the case may be, with a fancy or other descriptive name approved by
Government .and printed, inscribed or written in type not larger than, and in
the same colour as, the word "Margarine", "Banaspati" or "Charbini",
as the case may be.

Banaspati, margarine or charbi not to be sold loose

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
II‑GENERAL PROVISIONS
10. Banaspati, margarine or charbini not to be sold loose.‑No person
shall sell banaspati, margarine or charbini loose or from an open package.

Licence for manufacture, storage and sale of goods

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
II‑GENERAL PROVISIONS
11. Place used for certain purposes in connection with margarine, banaspati
or charbini; butter and ghee to be licenced.‑(1) No place shall be used‑
(a) for the large‑scale manufacture or preparation of
margarine, banaspati or charbini ;
(b) for the business of a wholesale dealer in margarine, banaspati or charbini ;
(c) as a butter or ghee
factory, that is to say, premises in which for purposes of trade, butter or
ghee is blended, reworked or subjected to any other treatment but not so as to
convert it into any substance other than butter or ghee ;
(d) as a creamery, a dairy or a backery ; and
(e) as a food processing, preserving, refrigerating, canning or
bottling factory except under a licence to be granted in such manner as may be
prescribed;
Provided that Government may
exempt from the operation of this section any premises or class of premises
described in clause (c).
(2) No place shall be used as a butter or ghee factory if it forms
part of or communicates otherwise than by a public street or road with any
other place which is required to be licensed under clause (a) or (b) of sub section
(1).

Register for manufacture and wholesale business

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
II‑GENERAL PROVISIONS
12. Registers to be kept by manufacturers and wholesale dealers.‑(1)
)every occupier of a place used for the preparation or manufacture for the purposes of trade of butter, ghee,
margarine, banaspati, charbini, cream,
milk or milk products, bakery products, confectionery, canned, bottled,
preserved, processed or refrigerated foods, or any other foods notified by
Government, and every wholesale dealer or his agent who 'stores any of the
aforesaid articles, shall keep and maintain a register in the form prescribed
showing the quantity and destination of each consignment of any such article
received or sent out from his place or premises of manufacture or business and such
register shall be open to inspection by the Inspector or any officer of the
Food Authority authorised in the manner prescribed, or by the Director or an
officer authorised by the Director.
(2) Every such occupier or wholesale dealer or his agent shall‑----
(a) produce the register for inspection when required to do so by
the Director or Inspector or any other officer under subsection (1) ;
(b) keep the register up‑to‑date ; and shall not‑
(i) wilfully make any entry in
the register which is false in any material particular ; or
(ii) fraudulently omit to enter
any, particulars which ought to be entered in the register.

Food poisoning

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
II‑GENERAL PROVISIONS
13. Prevention of food poisoning.‑(1) If the Health Officer
of a Food Authority has reasonable grounds for suspecting that any food of
which he or any other authorised Inspector has procurred a sample for analysis
under the provisions of this Ordinance is likely to cause food poisoning, he
may give notice to the person incharge of the food that until the investiga tion
is completed the food or any specified portion thereof shall not be used for
human consumption, and shall be kept or removed in the manner specified in the
notice.
(2) If the Health Officer of a
Food Authority has reasons to suspect that tuberculosis is caused or is likely
to be caused, by the consumption of milk supplied from any dairy or other
source, the Food Authority may, by notice to the person in charge of such dairy
or source, prohibit the supply of milk from such dairy or source.

Appointment of public analysts

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
III.‑ANALYSIS OF FOOD
14. Appointment of Analyst.‑Government may, by notification,
appoint Public Analysts for the purposes of this Ordinance, for the whole or
any part of the Province, for any specified food or generally for all foods.

Local authorities to enforce the ordinance

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
III.‑ANALYSIS OF FOOD
15. Appointment of Food Authorities.‑(1) The local authority
concerned shall be the Food Authority within the area under its jurisdiction.
(2) It shall be the duty of
every Food Authority to carry into execution and enforce the provisions of this
Ordinance within its jurisdiction with a view that all articles of food and
drink are sold in a pure and genuine state.

Appointment of inspectors

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
III.‑ANALYSIS OF FOOD
16. Appointment of Inspectors.‑(1) The Director, may, and
subject to any rules made by Government in this behalf, each Food Authority
shall for the area under its jurisdiction, appoint persons to be Inspectors,
either specifically for any specified food or generally for all foods;
Provided that the Health
Officer of a local authority shall be an ex‑officio
Inspector in respect of all foods within the area under its jurisdiction.
(2) An Inspector appointed by
the Director under the provisions of subsection (1) may exercise the powers and
perform the functions of an Inspector under this Ordinance throughout the
Province or in such area as the Director
may direct.
(3) An Inspector appointed by a
Food Authority under the provisions of subsection (1) may exercise the powers
and perform the functions of an Inspector under this Ordinance throughout the
area over which such Food Authority has jurisdiction or in such part of such
area as the Authority may by notification direct.
(4) The Director may exercise
the powers and perform the functions of an Inspector under this Ordinance
throughout the Province, and any Deputy or Assistant Director working under him
may exercise such powers and perform such functions throughout such areas as
the Director may by notification direct.

General powers of inspectors

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
III.‑ANALYSIS OF FOOD
17. General powers of Inspectors.‑(1) An Inspector may detain
and search any vehicle or package of any food intended for sale or in the
course of delivery if he has reason to suspect that the food therein carried or
contained may be injurious to health, unwholesome or unfit for human
consumption or is not of the same nature, substance or quality which it
purports to be;
Provided that nothing in this
section shall authorise the detention of any vehicle belonging to the Railways.
(2) An Inspector may at such
time as may be prescribed‑
(i) enter into and inspect any
market, godown, shop, stall or other place used for the sale of any food
intended for human consumption or for the preparation, manufacture or storage
of any such food for the purposes of trade or sale ;
(ii) enter upon any premises
for the purposes of exercising the powers of purchasing or taking a sample
under section 18 and may in such premises inspect and examine any food and any
apparatus, utensil or vessel used for preparing, manufacturing or containing
such food.
(3) If any such food as is
mentioned in subsection (1) or clause (ii) of subsection (2) appears to the
Inspector to be injurious to health, unwholesome, unfit for human consumption,
not of the same nature, substance or quality which it purports to be or not
fulfilling the prescribed conditions subject to which such food is to be
manufactured, sold, kept or stored, or if any such apparatus, utensil or vessel
as is mentioned in clause (ii) of subsection (2) is of such kind or in such
state as to render any food prepared, manufactured or contained therein
unwholesome or unfit for human consumption or injurious to health, he may seize
and remove such food or apparatus, utensil or vessel so as to be dealt with as
hereinafter provided.
(4) An Inspector may, instead
of removing such food, apparatus, utensil or vessel seized under subsection
(3), leave the same in the custody of the person from whose possession, custody
or control the same was seized or in such safe custody as he may deem fit, so
as to be dealt with as hereinafter provided; and he may, at any time thereafter
remove the same to the custody of the Food Authority concerned.
(5) (a) When any food,
apparatus, utensil or vessel is seized ‑ under subsection (3), it may be
destroyed by the officer making the seizure with the consent of the owner or
the person in whose possession, custody or control it is found.
(b) If any food seized is of a
perishable nature and is in the opinion of the officer making the seizure,
unsound, unwholesome or unfit for human consumption or not of the same nature,
substance or quality which it purports to be, it may, with the previous
permission of the officer authorised in this behalf by the Food Authority, be
destroyed without such consent.
(6) An Inspector seizing any
food, apparatus, utensil or vessel under subsection (3) shall prepare a
statement describing the food,, apparatus, utensil or vessel so seized and
shall, if the person from whose possession, custody or control the same is
seized be present at the time of seizure. deliver a copy of the said statement
to him or, if he be not so present, send such copy to him by registered post.
(7) (a) Any person claiming
anything seized under subsection (3) may within seven days of the seizure
complain to any Magistrate of the first or second class having jurisdiction at
the place of seizure, who, after making such enquiry as he may deem necessary,
may either confirm or disallow such seizure wholly or in part or may order the
article to be restored to the claimant.
(b) If the Magistrate confirms
the seizure, the food, apparatus, utensil or vessel, as the case may be, shall
be forfeited to the Food Authority concerned or the Magistrate may direct that
such food, apparatus, utensil or vessel may be destroyed or disposed of at the
cost of

Purchase of samples, etc.

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
III.‑ANALYSIS OF FOOD
18. Power to demand, select and take samples.‑(1) An.
Inspector may, for the purpose of analysis, purchase or procure, upon tendering
the pre vailing market price, a sample of food‑----
(a) in transit,
(b) sold or manufactured or
intended to be sold or manufactured, kept or stored or received for the purpose
of preparing therewith any food,
(c) kept or stored in a market,
godown, shop, stall, hotel, restaurant or eating house for the purpose of trade
or sale or received therein for the purpose of preparing therewith any food.
(2) On a demand being made by
an Inspector in this behalf, the person in charge of such food shall be bound
to give a sample of the same.
Explanation.‑The purchase
or sale of a sample of any food under the provisions of this Ordinance for the
purposes of analysis shall be deemed to be purchased or sale of such food for
human consumption or use unless the seller proves that the bulk from which such
sample was taken was not offered, exposed or intended for sale for human
consumption or use.
(3) If any person fails to give
a sample as provided under subsection (2) the Inspector may, without prejudice
to any penalty prescribed by or under this Ordinance, seize such quantity of
the food as may be necessary and shall give him a certificate, showing the
price, nature and quantity of the food seized and the date, time and place of
seizure, and on demand being made in that behalf, the price of the food seized.
(4) An Inspector while taking a
sample under subsection (1) shall prepare
a declaration in duplicate in the form specified in First Schedule containing
full particulars relating to the sample in question, to he given by the person
from whom the sample is taken, and the declaration so prepared shall be signed
or marked both by the Inspector and the person from whom the said declaration is taken.
(5) When a sample is taken from
the stock in the possession of a commission agent, such agent shall be bound,
on demand by the Inspector, to state forthwith the name and all such
particulars known to him as may be required of or concerning the person on
whose behalf such stock is held by such agent.

Right of private persons to have samples analysed

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
III.‑ANALYSIS OF FOOD
19. Right of private persons to
have samples analysed.‑Any
person may require any, Inspector to purchase a sample of any food, in
accordance with the provisions of section 18 and to submit the same for
analysis.

Methods of taking samples

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
III.‑ANALYSIS OF FOOD
20. Methods of taking samples.‑(1) An Inspector after
purchasing or procuring or seizing any food with the intention of submitting
the same for analysis shall, forthwith, divide the food in three parts to be
then and there separated and each part shall be marked, sealed or fastened in
such manner as the nature of the case will permit ; and the person from whom
the sample is taken may, if he so desires, also affix his seal or mark on each
of the three parts.
(2) An Inspector shall‑
(a) if required to do so,
deliver one part to the person from whom the article is purchased or seized or
the sample is taken ;
(b) retain one part for future comparison ; and
(c) submit one part to the
Public Analyst;
Provided that where the sample
is taken from any food which is about to be imported or is in transit or at the
place of delivery to the purchaser, consumer or consignee or is unclaimed, the
first‑mentioned part of the sample shall be retained by the Inspector,
unless the name and address of the consignor appear on the container containing
the article sampled, in which case he shall forward that part to the consignor
by registered post or other wise, together with a notice informing that person
that the sample would be analysed by the Public Analyst.

Certificate of analysts

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
III.‑ANALYSIS OF FOOD
21. Certificate of Analyst.‑(1)
The Public Analyst upon receiving any food or a sample of food from the
Inspector shall, as soon as possible, analyse the same and deliver or send to
the Inspector forwarding the sample, on payment of such fees as may be
prescribed, a certificate in the form specified in the Second Schedule showing
the result of the analysis.
(2) Where any method has been
prescribed by rules made under this Ordinance for the analysis of any food,
every Public Analyst shall, in his certificate of analysis, declare that he has
followed the prescribed method in his analysis.
(3) A copy of such certificate
may be obtained from the Public Analyst by the person from whom the article so
analysed was purchased or obtained on payment of a fee of two rupees.
(4) No person shall display any
such copy on his premises or use such copy as an advertisement.

Power of Government to have articles analysed

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
III.‑ANALYSIS OF FOOD
22. Power of Government to have articles analysed.‑Government may, in
relation to any matter appearing to it to affect the general interests of the
consumers of any food, direct any public servant to procure for analysis,
samples of such food and thereupon such public servant shall have all the
powers of an Inspector under this Ordinance;
Provided that‑--
(a) the public servant upon
receiving the certificate of the Public Analysit shall take proceedings or
cause proceedings to be taken as if he himself had caused such analysis to be
made ;
(b) any fee prescribed for such analysis, the‑ cost of the
sample and the expenditure incurred in procuring it, including the travelling
allowance, if any, of the public servant procuring the same shall be payable by
the Food Authority of the area from where the sample is procured.

Penalties

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART IV‑PENALTIES AND PROCEDURE
23. Penalties.‑(1) Whoever contravenes the provisions of sections
3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11 or 13 shall be punished;
(a) for a first offence with
imprisonment which may extend to one year and fine ;
(b) for a second offence with imprisonment which may extend to two
years and fine ; provided that in the absence of special reasons to the
contrary to be recorded in the judgment of the Court such imprisonment shall
not be less than three months.
(2) Whoever‑
(a) contravenes the provisions
of section 10 or 12, or
(b) displays a certificate of a
Public Analyst or Chemical Examiner in contravention of the provisions of
subsection (4) of section 21, or
(c) contravenes the provisions
of any rule made under this Ordinance not coming within the scope of subsection
(1), shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to one year or with
fine or with both.

sections.description:
Presumption

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART IV‑PENALTIES AND PROCEDURE
24. Presumption.‑In every
prosecution under this Ordinance relating to any food the Court shall presume‑‑
(a) that any food found in
possession of any person, who is or has been habitually found manufacturing,
selling, keeping, storing, offering or exposing for sale or hawking about such
food, was being manufactured, sold, kept, stored, offered or exposed for sale
or hawked about by such person ;
(b) that any food commonly used for human consumption is sold, kept
or stored for human consumption ;
(c) that any food commonly used
for human consumption, which is found on premises used for the preparation or
manufacture of such food, was intended to be prepared or manufactured for human
consumption ;
(d) that any substance capable
of being used in the manufacture or preparation of any food commonly used for
human consumption, which is found on premises in which such food is
manufactured or prepared, was intended to be used in the manufacture or
preparation of such food ;
(e) that any food is not of the nature, substance or quality it
purports to be, if it is deficient in any of its normal constituents to the
extent specified in the rules made under this Ordinance or if any extraneous
matter has been added to it in contravention of such rules.

Declaration under section 18 to be evidence

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART IV‑PENALTIES AND PROCEDURE
25. Declaration under section 18 to be evidence.‑A declaration
signed or marked under subsection (4) of section 18 may be produced as evidence
of the facts contained therein in any enquiry, trial or other proceedings under
this Ordinance.

Certificate of public analyst to be evidence of fact therein stated

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART IV‑PENALTIES AND PROCEDURE
26. Certificate of Public
Analyst to be evidence of fact
therein stated. (1) The production in any enquiry, trial or other
proceedings under this Ordinance of a certificate under the hand of a Public
Analyst in the form specified in the Second Schedule shall, until the contrary
is proved, be sufficient evidence of the facts therein stated.
(2) When any person is accused
of an offence under this Ordinance, he may require the Court to summon as a
witness the Public Analyst who analysed the, food or sample of food in respect
of which he is accused of having committed an offence and the Court may, and
shall, in every case in which the accused deposits in the Court a sum of money
in accordance with the scale prescribed, summon the Public Analyst, and if such
person is acquitted, any sum of money so deposited shall be refunded to him.

Analysis by chemical examiner

WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960

27. Analysis by Chemical Examiner.‑(1) The Court may of its
own accord or on the request of the accused cause any food or sample of food to
be sent for analysis to the Chemical Examiner to Government, who shall
thereupon with all convenient speed analyse the same and report the result of
the analysis to the Court in the form specified in the. Second Schedule, and
the cost of such analysis shall be paid by the accused if the Court so directs.
(2) The certificate of the
Chemical Examiner to Government shall, until the contrary is proved, be
sufficient evidence of the facts therein stated, but if the Court considers it
necessary in the interests of justice it may summon him to give evidence in
connection with the certificate issued by him, and in such a case the cost of
summoning the Chemical Examiner to Government shall be paid by the accused or
the Food Authority as the Court may direct,
(3) The provisions of subsection
(4) of section 21 shall apply in respect of the report of the Chemical
Examiner.

What is or is not a good defence in a prosecution under the ordinance

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART IV‑PENALTIES AND PROCEDURE
28. What is or is not a good defence
in a prosecution under the Ordinance.‑(1) In any prosecution under
this Ordinance relating to any food it shall be no defence to allege‑
(a) that the accused was ignorant of the nature, substance or
quality of the food, or
(b) that the purchaser having bought only for analysis was not
prejudiced.
'(2). The seller shall not be
deemed to have committed an offence under this Ordinance if he proves‑
(a) that the food sold was purchased or obtained as agent by him as
being of the same nature, substance or quality as that demanded by the
purchaser and with written warranty to the effect that it was of such nature,
substance or quality ;
(b) that he had no reason to
believe at the time when he sold it that the food was not of such nature,
substance or quality as required ; and
(c) that he sold it in the same
state in which he purchased it.
(3) No evidence of a warranty
under clause (a) of subsection (2) shall be admissible on behalf of the
seller‑
(a) unless the seller has within seven days of the service of the
summons upon him sent to the Inspector a copy of the warranty (together with a
translation thereof in English) with a notice stating that he intends to rely
on it and specifying the name and address of the person from whom he received
it and has also sent a like notice of his intention to that person ; and
(b). unless such warranty is given by a person permanently residing
or carrying on business in Pakistan.

Forfeiture of food upon conviction

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART IV‑PENALTIES AND PROCEDURE
29. Forfeiture of food upon conviction.‑In
the case of any conviction under this Ordinance the convicting Magistrate .may
order that any food to which the conviction relates, together with all packages
or vessels containing the same, shall be confiscated to Government and disposed
of as the Magistrate may direct.

Expenses of analysis to be paid by the offenders on conviction

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART IV‑PENALTIES AND PROCEDURE
30. Expenses of analysis to
be paid by offenders on conviction.‑When any person is convicted of
an offence under this Ordinance, the convicting Magistrate shall order that all
fees and other expenses incidental to the analysis of any food in respect of
which the conviction is made, which shall in no case be less than thirty
rupees, be paid by the person convicted, in addition to the fine, if any, which
he may be sentenced to pay and the amount of such fees and expenses may be
recovered as if it were a fine.

Offences under the ordinance not to be tried by a Magistrate exercising lesser powers than Magistrate of the first class

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART IV‑PENALTIES AND PROCEDURE
31. Offences under the Ordinance not be tried by a Magistrate exercising lesser powers than Magistrate of the second class.‑No offence under this
Ordinance or the rules made thereunder shall be triable by a Magistrate
exercising powers less than those of a Magistrate of the second class.

32. Complaint to be filed by
whom.‑No Court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under
this Ordinance except on a report in writing of the facts constituting such
offence made by an Inspector authorised in this behalf by a general or special
order of the Director.

33. Liability for acts done in good faith in discharge of duty or exercise of powers.‑No person
shall be liable to any penalty or payment of damages on account of any act done
in good faith in pursuance of any duty imposed or authority conferred by any
provision of this Ordinance or of any rule, order or direction lawfully made or
given thereunder.

" 34. Inspector to be
deemed public servant.‑An
Inspector while exer cising any of the functions conferred upon him by or under
this Ordinance and all other persons assisting. him in discharging such
functions shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of section
21 of the Pakistan Penal Code.

Power of Government to appoint a public servant to exercise the functions of any local authority

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
V‑MISCELLANEOUS
35. Power of Government to appoint a public
servant to exercise the functions
of any Food Authority.‑(1) If
the Deputy Commissioner of a district receives information from the Director or
has reason to believe that a Food Authority has failed to execute or enforce
any of the provisions of this Ordinance in relation to any food and that the
failure effects the general interest of the consumers, he may, after making
such enquiry from the Food Authority as he thinks fit, by order, empower any
public servant to execute or enforce these provisions or to procure the
execution or enforcement thereof in relation to such food and the order may fix
a reasonable remuneration to be paid to such public servant, and such
remuneration together with any expenses incurred by the public servant in
performing the duties of the Food Authority under this Ordinance shall be paid
by the local authority.
(2) If the expenses and
remuneration are not so paid the Deputy Commissioner may make an order
directing any person who for the time being has custody of any moneys on behalf
of the local authority, as its officer; treasurer, banker or ' otherwise, to
pay such expenses and remuneration from such moneys as he may have in his hands
or may from time to time receive, and such person shall be bound to obey such
order.
(3) When the Deputy
Commissioner makes any order under this section, he shall forthwith forward to
the Commissioner and to the local authority affected thereby a copy of the
order with a statement of the reasons for making it, and it shall be in the
discretion of the Commissioner to rescind the order, or to direct that it my
continue in force with or without modi fications.
(4) The Commissioner shall
forthwith submit to Government a report of every case occurring under this
section, and Government may confirm, revise or modify the order, or make in
respect thereof any other order which the Commissioner could have made
Provided that no order of the
Deputy Commissioner or the Commis sioner passed under this section shall be
confirmed, revised or modified by Government without giving the local authority
a reasonable opportunity of showing cause against such order.

36. Delegation.‑Government
may delegate all or any of its powers and functions under this Ordinance to the
Director or any other officer by name or designation.

Power to make rules

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
V‑MISCELLANEOUS
37. Power to make rules.‑(1)
Government may frame rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the
provisions of this Ordinance.
(2) In particular and without
prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power, Government may frame rules‑
(a) prescribing the
qualifications of persons who may be appointed Public Analysts for the purpose
of this Ordinance ;
(b) regulating the appointment and qualifications of persons to be
appointed as Inspectors under this Ordinance ;
(c) prescribing the methods of
analysis to be followed by Public Analysts for the analysis of any food ;
(d) fixing the fees to be paid
in respect of the analysis of any food by a Public Analyst ;
(e) prohibiting the use of any
particular matter or ingredient in the manufacture or preparation of any food ;
(f) specifying the conditions
(which include the addition of a colour or any other substance) subject to
which any food shall be manufactured, sold, kept stored, offered or exposed for
sale ;
(g) prohibiting the keeping or storage of foods other than those
approved under the rules ;
(h) securing the cleanliness
and freedom from contamination of any food in the course of its manufacture,
preparation, storage, packing, carriage, delivery or exposure for sale, and
securing the cleanliness of places, receptacles, packages, wrappings,
appliances and vehicles used in such manufacture, pre paration, storage,
packing, carriage or delivery;
(i) prescribing the method in
which labels shall be affixed, languages in which the labels shall be printed
and the symbols which shall be used for different kinds of foods ;
(j) prescribing the manner in
which, and the conditions subject to which, a licence is to be granted under
section 11 ;
(k) prescribing the form, and
the particulars to be entered in the register to be kept under section 12 ;
(l) authorising at person
taking a sample of milk or any other food for the purpose of analysis to add
preservatives to such samples for maintaining it in a suitable condition for
analysis and regulating the nature and method of addition of such preservatives
;
(m) prohibiting the use or
addition as a preservative of any article, material or substance in the
manufacture or preparation for sale of any food;
(n) prescribing the fees which a local authority may levy for the
grant of a licence ;and
(o) prescribing the fees to be
deposited in Court for summoning a Public Analyst.

Repeal and savings

ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
ORDINANCE VII OF 1960
WEST PAKISTAN PURE FOOD ORDINANCE, 1960
PART
V‑MISCELLANEOUS
38. Repeal and savings.‑(1) The following enactments are
hereby repealed :‑
(a) the Punjab Pure Food Act, 1929 ;
(b) the Punjab Pure Food Act, 1929, in its application to the
territories which formed the North‑West Frontier Province before the
establishment of West Pakistan ;
(c) the Bahawalpure State Pure
Food Act, 1946 ;
(d) the Sind Foods Act, 1947 ;
(e) the Khairpur Prevention of Adulteration Act, 1941 ;
(f) the North‑West
Frontier Province Artificial Ghee Colourization Act, 1939.
(2) Notwithstanding the repeal
of the enactments mentioned in sub section (1), everything done and all action
taken, obligation, liability, penalty or punishment incurred, inquiry or proceeding
commenced, officer appointed or person authorised, jurisdiction or power
conferred, rule made and notifica tion issued under any provisions of the said
enactments shall, if not inconsistent with the provisions of this Ordinance,
continue in force and be deemed to have been respectively done, taken,
incurred, commenced, appointed, authorised, conferred, made or issued under
this Ordinance.
(3) The areas to which any of
the enactments enumerated in sub‑section (1) applied before the
commencement of this Ordinance shall be considered to have been duly notified
under subsection (3) of section 1 of this Ordinance.
